# Blackbody Radiation **The Planck curve emerges from collisions — no energy quanta assumed.** Particles bounce in a walled cavity. The frequency histogram converges to the Planck distribution. No discrete energy quanta, no Planck's constant inserted — the quantization is a consequence of the discrete pixel/tick lattice. Classically this is supposed to produce the Rayleigh-Jeans divergence (infinite energy at high frequencies); the discrete lattice cuts it off and yields the Planck curve instead. *New to FRQTL? Start with **Hello, FRQTL** (`getting-started-hello-frqtl`) for the `caps.frqtl` setup-module + declarative-canvas basics this notebook assumes.* The scene — the blackbody scene's sketch file, verbatim: a bounce-walled oven cavity with its thermostat, a radiation slit and an absorbing sink — as editable user code. Its first statement creates the world (`exp.createCanvas`): /* Copyright 2023-2026 by Essam Abadir */ /** * SCENE — Blackbody * * A sketch file: the WHOLE scene as one ES module, `export default function buildExperiment(exp)`. The world, the * oven, its thermostat and the radiation sink are all constructed here; the sugar objects * (OvenBox, LargeObject), the renderer and the engine are imports. A row of * egpt-frqtl's roster (rung blackbody). * * Physics (zero new — composition of goldened behaviours): a cavity of absorbing walls holds a * population of leaves; the OvenBox thermostat keeps the cavity's quanta near the TEMPERATURE * target by emitting, and colliding leaves merge into parent frames (bench H2a–c, * collide → merge → promote; `withInterQuantumCollisions`). A parent's fullness IS its frequency * (wavelength = capacity/mass, bench M4), so what leaks out of the slit in the right wall is a * spectrum of frame sizes — the emergent Planck-like curve — with no energy quanta assumed. * Everything that escapes is absorbed by the sink at the right edge (the experiment boundary). * * Order matters (it seeds the run): the world, the brownian/collision flags, the quantum * layer, the thermostat SLOT (reserved before the oven so the oven's own tick-fns run after it), * the oven, the thermostat, the sink. Same calls, same order, same seed ⇒ the same RNG stream. */ import { CollisionActions, CollisionTypes, FrqtlControlOverlay, FrqtlControlsPanel, LargeObject, Rectangle } from '@descix/frqtl-web/parts'; import * as ControlRegistry from '@descix/frqtl-web/shim/controls/registry.js'; const W = 600, H = 400; // THE WORLD this scene states (its co-init call below) const SINK_DEPTH = 30; // the absorbing strip at the right canvas edge (px) export const parts = { // ── THE SINK — the experiment boundary on the slit side ───────────────── radiation_sink: [LargeObject, { rect: { left: W - SINK_DEPTH, top: 0, w: SINK_DEPTH, h: H }, collision_type: CollisionTypes.NONE, actions: [CollisionActions.ABSORB], reposition: 'closest', color: [0, 0, 0] }], }; export default function buildExperiment(exp) { var TEMPERATURE = 1500; // target quanta inside the cavity (the knob below) var QUANTUM_DIM = 3; // the layer leaves promote into: an 8 px box edge, 64 cells of capacity in 2D var BOX_FRACTION = 1 / 3; // the cavity's outer box, as a fraction of the canvas var WALL = 10; // wall thickness (px) var SLIT_HEIGHT = 60; // the radiation slit in the right wall (px) // ── WORLD — a 2D canvas + universe, fundamental layer 0 (1x1 leaves), λ multiplier 1 ── exp.createCanvas(W, H, { dimension: 0, wavelengthScale: 1 }); var u = exp.universe; u.brownianMotion = true; u.withInterQuantumCollisions = true; u.addDimension(QUANTUM_DIM); // ── THE OVEN — the cavity, centred on the canvas ──────────────────────── var outer = new Rectangle(Math.round(W / 2), Math.round(H / 2), Math.round(W * BOX_FRACTION), Math.round(H * BOX_FRACTION), null, true); // The thermostat runs FIRST each tick: reserve its slot before the oven registers its own. var thermostatSlot = u.experimentTickFunctions.length; u.experimentTickFunctions.push(null); var oven = exp.addObject('OvenBox', { name: 'oven', left: outer.left + WALL, top: outer.top + WALL, width: outer.w - 2 * WALL, height: outer.h - 2 * WALL, wallThickness: WALL, temperature: TEMPERATURE, slitHeight: SLIT_HEIGHT, // the slit is in the RIGHT wall (OvenBox's own slit side) color: [120, 120, 120] }); u.experimentTickFunctions[thermostatSlot] = oven.getTemperatureTickFunction(); exp.declare(parts); // the sink (parts.radiation_sink) // ── THE KNOB — temperature, live (the oven's own thermostat target) ───── var registry = ControlRegistry.makeControlRegistry(); registry.registerControls('blackbody', [ { kind: 'scalar', id: 'temperature', label: 'temperature (quanta)', min: 50, max: 8000, step: 50, value: TEMPERATURE, fmt: function (v) { return String(v); }, onChange: function (v) { oven.setTemperature(v); }, place: { x: 0.02, y: 0.03 } } ]); // Chrome (a page only): expose the knobs to a host frame, and mount the overlay through the // runner's ONE door (runner.controlHost) — before a canvas is mounted (a notebook pane) there is // none, so the knobs stay in the exposed registry only. FrqtlControlsPanel.exposeRegistry(registry, { runner: exp.runner }); if (exp.runner.controlHost) { FrqtlControlOverlay.mount(exp.runner, { registry: registry, name: 'blackbody' }); } } Declare a `shape="recipe"` canvas that runs it: `setup=""` + `seed` — no `stage`, because the scene states its own world in its first statement. Click **Run** (or **Run All**): ## What you are seeing Particles bounce within the cavity, exchanging momentum on every collision. Energy redistributes across the population until the frequency distribution stabilizes — the emergent shape matches the Planck curve, not the diverging Rayleigh-Jeans prediction. **`TEMPERATURE` is the driving knob** (the scene's constant, 1500 here). It sets the thermostat's target `activeQuanta` count. The thermostat emits `floor((temperature - activeQuanta) / 4)` new leaf Frames per emitter per tick until the target is met, then silences all emitters that tick — a discrete proportional controller over quanta count. Raising `temperature` 300 → 4000 densifies the cavity from sparse scattered leaf dots to a near-saturated mass, increases compound-frame (non-leaf, merged) formation dramatically, and widens the escaped-radiation stream through the slit in both volume and angular spread. The sweep was captured. Note: `temperature` is NOT energy or kinetic temperature in the continuous-mechanics sense — it is the integer target for `universe.activeQuanta`. The per-Frame oscillation wavelength (`wavelength = floor((capacity / mass) × WAVELENGTH_CONSTANT)`, Core Axiom §6) is unchanged by `temperature` directly; it is determined by the mass of each Frame, which grows as frames merge via collisions. Higher temperature → more collisions → larger compound frames → shorter oscillation wavelengths — the FRAQTL analog of Wien's displacement. **Edit the physics:** open the `./setups/blackbody.js` tab, change one of the scene's constants — e.g. `var TEMPERATURE = 1500;` → `3000` (also try `SLIT_HEIGHT` or `BOX_FRACTION`) — and re-Run. The emergent frequency spectrum changes because you edited the construction, not a label. The simulation runs live in your browser on the compiled FRQTL (WASM) engine.
